title: A low-cost and open-source protocol to produce key enzymes for molecular detection assays
protocol: Sterilize the media by autoclaving at 15 psi and 121°C for 15 min.
Cool down the media to approximately 45°C.
Add 30 μg/mL Kan and 17 μg/mL Cam to 2.2 L of LB broth for Taq and RT enzymes.
Prepare 1.2 L of LB broth with 100 μg/mL Amp for Cas12a enzyme expression.
Prepare 1.2 L LB broth with 100 μg/mL Amp and 30 μg/mL Cam for Tev enzyme expression.
Transfer a freshly transformed colony to a 250 mL flask containing 50 mL of LB with appropriate selection antibiotic(s).
Incubate at 37°C for 14–16 hours with shaking at 150 RPM.
Inoculate 1 L of fresh media (LB with the corresponding antibiotics) with the starter culture to reach an OD600 of 0.05.
Incubate at 37°C with shaking at 150 RPM until OD600 = 0.5 (1.5 h) for Tev and LbCas12a or OD600 = 0.8 for Taq and RT (2 h).
Take a 200 μL sample for pre-induction monitoring.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of 1 mM and incubate at 37°C for 3 h at 150 RPM for Taq, Tev, and RT.
Incubate on ice or at 4°C for 10–15 min for Cas12a.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.2 mM and incubate at 22°C-25°C for 14-16 h at 150 RPM for Cas12a.
Measure the OD600 and take 200 μL of culture at 2–3-time intervals (each hour for Taq, Tev, and RT).
Take a sample before cell harvest (store on ice) for Cas12a.
Keep culture samples on ice.
Keep flasks with induced cultures on ice.
Use 50 mL conical tubes for collecting cells.
Avoid loading more than 45 mL of cell culture in each tube.
Centrifuge the culture at 3000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash cells with 10 mL per gram of cell pellet weight using TAKM or HAKM buffer.
Gently resuspend until the pellet is homogenized.
Centrifuge at 3000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL per gram of cell pellet weight with the indicated buffers prepared with cOmplete™ protease inhibitor cocktail.
Add lysozyme at 100 μg/mL final concentration to the resuspended cells.
Add DNase I at 40 μg/mL final concentration to the resuspended cells.
Add MgCl2 at 10 mM final concentration to Taq, RT, and Tev resuspended cells.
Centrifuge the 200 μL samples obtained before induction and during induction at 3000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellets with SDS sample buffer as follows: SDS sample buffer (μL) = OD600 * Cell Vol μL / 2
Heat the SDS-treated samples at 95°C for 10 min.
Run a polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) using 15 μL of each sample.
Use 10% SDS-PAGE for Taq and RT samples.
Use 7.5% SDS-PAGE for Cas12a samples.
Use 12.5% SDS-PAGE for Tev samples.
Run the gel for 5 min at 100 V followed by 55 min at 200 V.
Stain the gel using Coomassie blue dye or other alternatives available.
Destain the gel by incubating it in 80 mL of destaining solution at 22°C–25°C with agitation for 3 h.
Change the destaining solution several times until most of the Coomassie blue dye is removed from the gel matrix.
Use two or three freeze-thaw cycles for cell lysis.
Thaw the frozen cell resuspension on ice and manually mix every 3 min.
Re-freeze it at -80°C for 15 min once thawed.
Thaw it again at 4°C on ice, mixing every 3 min.
Adjust NaCl concentration to 370 mM using a 4 M stock for M-MLV reverse transcriptase (RT).
Mix gently the adjusted RT solution.
Adjust to 20 mL per gram of cell pellet weight with MB1 buffer containing 370 mM NaCl.
Centrifuge at 11000 × g for 45 min at 4°C for M-MLV RT.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL tube after centrifuging M-MLV RT solution.
Maintain the clarified lysate at 4°C for M-MLV RT.
Heat the lysis suspension at 80°C for one hour for Taq DNA polymerase.
Adjust to 20 mL per gram of cell pellet weight with TaB1 buffer after heating the lysis suspension for Taq DNA polymerase.
Add glycerol to a final concentration of 10% in the solution for Taq DNA polymerase.
Add imidazole to a final concentration of 10 mM (use a 2 M stock solution, pH 8.0) for Taq DNA polymerase.
Add β-mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 6 mM for Taq DNA polymerase.
Centrifuge at 11000 × g for 45 min at 4°C after adding reagents for Taq DNA polymerase.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL tube after centrifuging Taq DNA polymerase solution.
Maintain the clarified lysate at 4°C after transferring the supernatant of Taq DNA polymerase.
Centrifuge at 11000 × g for 45 min at 4°C for LbCas12a and TEV protease.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL tube after centrifuging LbCas12a and TEV protease solution.
Maintain the clarified lysate at 4°C after transferring the supernatant of LbCas12a and TEV protease.
Avoid freezing or storing crude lysates.
Filter the supernatant with a 0.45 μm syringe filter before purification.
Remove the storage solution from the HisTrap FF Crude column using 10 column volumes (CV) of ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with 10 CV of MB1 buffer.
Filter the clarified supernatant with a 0.45 μm filter to avoid column clogging.
Load the filtered sample onto the column.
Collect the flow-through in 15 mL conical tubes.
Keep all purification intermediates until SDS-PAGE analysis.
Prepare a 20 μL sample of each step with SDS sample buffer during pauses.
Wash the column with 10 CV of MB2 buffer followed by 10 CV of MB1 buffer.
Collect washes in 15 mL conical tubes.
Elute the protein with 8 mL of MB3 buffer.
Collect elution fractions in 0.5 mL volumes in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Clean the column with 20 CV of MB1 buffer, followed by 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by 10% SDS-PAGE (100 V for 5 minutes followed by 200 V for 50 minutes).
Use Coomassie blue staining to visualize protein bands.
Identify the presence of protein in each fraction using absorbance at 280 nm or Bradford assay.
Select and pool fractions based on quantity and purity as seen in the results.
Dialyze using 1 L of MB4 buffer on ice for 16 ± 2 hours using a D-Tube™ dialyzer Maxi with MWCO from 12 to 14 kDa.
Calculate the ratio between recovered protein and total input protein by absorbance at 280 nm, Bradford assay, or pixel densitometry of the SDS-PAGE gel.
Centrifuge the collected protein from the dialyzer tube in 1.5 mL tubes at 15000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Remove storage solution (20% ethanol) from the HiTrap SP column with ultra-pure water, using a volume equivalent to ten times the column volume.
Equilibrate the HiTrap SP column with MB4 buffer, using a volume equivalent to ten times the column volume.
Load the RT protein sample purified by affinity chromatography onto the equilibrated HiTrap SP column.
Wash the loaded column with 10 CV of MB4 buffer and collect it in a 15 mL conical tube.
Set up an FPLC system gradient from 0% to 100% (in 20 CV) of MB5 buffer for elution.
Collect 0.5 mL fractions in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes during the elution step.
Quantify the protein by densitometry analysis using BSA as a standard or by the Bradford assay.
Store 20 μL aliquots at −80°C.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen or dry ice ethanol/methanol/isopropanol bath if available.
Remove the storage solution from the HisTrap FF Crude column with ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with TaB1 buffer.
Filter the clarified supernatant with a 0.45 μm filter and load it onto the column.
Collect the flow-through in conical 15 mL tubes.
Wash with TaB2 buffer followed by TaB3 buffer, collecting fractions in 15 mL conical tubes.
Elute the protein with TaB4 buffer, collecting 0.5 mL fractions in microcentrifuge tubes.
Clean the column with TaB1 buffer and ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by performing a 10% SDS-PAGE at 100 V for 5 minutes followed by 200 V for 50 minutes.
Use Coomassie blue staining to visualize protein bands.
Pool fractions based on quantity and purity for dialysis against 1 L of TaB5 buffer on ice or in a cold room at 4°C for 16 ± 2 hours using a D-Tube™ dialyzer Maxi with MWCO from 12 to 14 kDa.
Collect the protein from the dialyzer tube into 1.5 mL tubes.
Centrifuge the collected protein at 15000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Remove the storage solution (20% ethanol) from the HiTrap Heparin HP column with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with 10 CV of TaB5 buffer.
Load the column with the Taq protein sample purified by affinity chromatography.
Wash twice with 10 CV of TaB5 buffer.
Collect wash fractions in 15 mL conical tubes.
Set a gradient from 0% to 100% (i.e., 20 CV) of TaB6 buffer for elution using the FPLC system.
Collect 0.5 mL fractions in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes during elution.
Prepare 50 mL buffer stocks from 100 mM to 1 M NaCl (TaB6 buffer) by varying the NaCl concentration in 50 mM increments for manual mode.
Use 2 CV of each stock during elution if using manual mode.
Clean the column with 10 CV of TaB5 buffer, followed by 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by 10% SDS-PAGE at 100 V for 5 min and then 200 V for 50 min.
Pool fractions considering quantity and purity for dialysis against 1 L of TaB7 buffer (at 4°C or cold room if available) for 16 ± 2 h placing the protein in a D-Tube™ dialyzer Maxi.
Collect the protein from the dialyzer tube into 1.5 mL tubes, centrifuge at 15000 × g for 15 min at 4°C and transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Quantify the protein by densitometry analysis using BSA as a standard or by the Bradford assay.
Store 20 μL aliquots at -80°C.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen or dry ice ethanol/methanol/isopropanol bath if available.
Remove the storage solution (20% ethanol) from the HisTrap FF crude column (1 mL column volume) with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with 10 CV of CB1 buffer.
Filter the clarified supernatant with a 0.45 μm filter.
Load the sample on the column.
Collect the flow-through in 15 mL tubes.
Wash with 10 CV of CB2 buffer.
Wash with 10 CV of CB3 buffer.
Collect them in 15 mL conical tubes.
Elute the protein with 8 mL of CB4 buffer.
Collect 0.5 mL fractions in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Clean the column with 5 CV of CB2 buffer.
Clean the column with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by 7.5% SDS-PAGE.
Run SDS-PAGE at 100 V for 5 min followed by 200 V for 50 min.
Use Coomassie blue staining if necessary.
Pool the protein-containing fractions considering quantity and purity.
Add TEV protease to a final concentration of 2.21 μM.
Dialyze Tev-treated fractions of LbCas12a against 1 L of CB5 buffer on ice.
Centrifuge the dialyzed sample at 15000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Assess TEV protease cleavage performance and protein purity by 12.5% SDS-PAGE.
Use Coomassie blue for staining.
Remove storage solution from the MBPTrap HP column with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with 10 CV of CB6 buffer.
Load the Tev-treated protein onto the column and collect the flow-through fraction on ice.
Assess purification performance by 12.5% SDS-PAGE.
Use Coomassie blue for staining.
Wash the column with 10 CV of CB7 buffer to remove MBP.
Clean the column with 10 CV of CB6 buffer and 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Remove storage solution from HiTrap Capto SP ImpRes Sepharose column with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate column with 10 CV of CB6 buffer.
Load FT collected from MBPTrap HP to the column.
Wash with 10 CV of CB6 buffer and collect in a 15 mL conical tube.
Set gradient from 0% to 100% (20 CV) of CB8 buffer for elution step using FPLC system.
Collect 0.5 mL fractions during elution in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Clean column with 10 CV of CB8 buffer, then with 10 CV of CB6 buffer and finally with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by 7.5% SDS-PAGE (100 V for 5 min and 200 V for 50 min).
Pool fractions considering quantity and purity for dialysis against 1 L of CB9 buffer (or 4°C cold room if available) for 16 ± 2 h placing the protein in a D-Tube™ dialyzer Maxi.
Collect the protein from the dialyzer tube into 1.5 mL tubes, centrifuge at 15000 × g for 15 min at 4°C and transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Quantify the protein by densitometry analysis using BSA as a standard or by the Bradford assay.
Store 20 μL aliquots at −80°C.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen or dry ice ethanol/methanol/isopropanol bath if available.
Remove the storage solution from the HisTrap FF Crude column with ultra-pure water.
Equilibrate the column with TeB2 buffer.
Filter the clarified supernatant with a 0.45 μm filter and load the sample on the column.
Collect the flow-through in 15 mL tubes.
Wash with 10 CV of TeB3 buffer.
Collect the wash in 15 mL conical tubes.
Elute the protein with 20 CV of TeB4 buffer.
Collect 0.5 mL fractions in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Clean the column with 5 CV of TeB2 buffer.
Clean the column with 10 CV of ultra-pure water.
Store the column with 5 CV of 20% ethanol.
Assess purification performance by 12.5% SDS-PAGE.
Pool fractions considering quantity and purity.
Dialyze against 1 L of TeB5 buffer for 16 ± 2 h using a D-Tube™ dialyzer Maxi on ice or in a 4°C cold room.
Collect the protein from the dialyzer tube into 1.5 mL tubes.
Centrifuge at 15000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Quantify the protein by densitometry analysis using BSA as a standard or by the Bradford assay.
Store 20 μL aliquots at -80°C.
Digest post-dialysis pooled samples with TEV protease.
Load digested sample into the MBPTrap HP column.
Pool fractions resulting from buffer salt concentration gradient obtained from IEC for dialysis.
Analyze collected flow-through and washes as well as obtained fractions.
Use HisTrap FF column for affinity chromatography.
Analyze collected samples, column post-loading fractions, and washes by SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Visualize the SDS-PAGE gels using Coomassie blue staining.
Clean the pedestal with dH2O.
Apply 2 μL in the bottom pedestal arm, then lower the upper pedestal to form a liquid column.
Wait for a couple of minutes.
Wipe away the water from both pedestals using a clean wipe (i.e., Kimtech ScienceTM KimwipeTM).
Select the Protein A280 option and perform the blank reading using 1–2 μL of the respective storage buffer.
Raise the upper pedestal arm and clean the buffer from both upper and bottom measurement surfaces using a clean dry paper wipe.
Enter the sample name and select “E and MW” as sample type option to use the extinction coefficient and molecular weight of the protein to calculate the sample concentration.
Place 2 μL of the sample and measure in triplicates.
Calculate the average and standard deviation of the measurements.
Prepare at least five dilutions of the protein standard for gel quantification.
Mix each dilution with SDS sample buffer.
Heat diluted standard and protein samples at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Spin samples briefly after heating.
Prepare an SDS-PAGE gel according to the required percentage.
Load the standard and samples (100 V for 15 min followed by 200 V for 40 min).
Stain the gel with Coomassie blue dye or another method available.
Destain the gel matrix as described.
Visualize the protein bands.
Prepare five dilutions of the protein standard using storage buffer as a diluent.
Use a range between 15 – 250 μg/mL in 100 μL.
Prepare a blank with only storage buffer.
Prepare three 10 μL serial dilutions of the proteins (ratio 1/10 to 1).
Add 90 μL of Bradford reagent to each dilution.
Mix gently 3 to 5 times.
Incubate at 22°C–25°C for 5 min in the dark.
Read absorbance at 595 nm.
Normalize raw data by subtracting blank absorbance (storage buffer only).
Plot normalized absorbance against BSA concentration on a standard curve.
Determine unknown protein concentrations using linear regression of the standard curve.
Calculate sample concentration by interpolating corresponding Abs595 with the linear regression.
Multiply resulting concentrations by the dilution factor applied at step c.ii.
Average and calculate standard deviation for results.
Dilute the M-MLV reverse transcriptase enzyme stock in MB6 buffer to a final concentration of 34 ng/μL for a 20X working stock.
Dilute the Taq DNA polymerase enzyme stock in MB6 buffer to a final concentration of 32 ng/μL for a 20X working stock.
Prepare RT-PCR using positive and negative standardized controls.
Include a non-template negative control (NTC) in each assay.
Add nuclease-free water to the PCR tube for the NTC.
Run the RT-PCR program as specified.
Visualize RT-PCR products by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Use a percentage of agarose according to the expected RT-PCR product size (3–5%).
Incubate the crRNA re-folding mixture at 65°C for 10 min followed by cooling at 22°C–25°C for 10 min.
Prepare a 10X CRISPR-Cas12a complex according to specified recipe.
Incubate the 10X CRISPR-Cas12a complex at 22°C–25°C for 10 min, protecting it from light.
Add MgCl2 to the 1X CrB1 to achieve a final concentration of 17.65 mM in 1X CrB2.
Prepare the CRISPR/Cas assay according to specified scheme.
Incubate the CRISPR/Cas reaction at 22°C–25°C for 30 min without light exposure.
Transfer tubes to a blue transilluminator and close the filter tap.
Register results of direct fluorescence visualization using a photo camera or smartphone.
Use a black cabinet, box, or darkroom to improve direct visualization of the results.
Alternatively, use a fluorescence 96-well plate reader for measurements.
Excite fluorescence at 491 nm.
Measure fluorescence at 525 nm on a SynergyTM H1 Hybrid Multi-Mode plate reader (Biotek).
